clue.text: Crisis time — my fish supper costs less

definitions.meaning: a moment of reckoning when everything is at stake
read literally: the price of the fried potatoes with the fish has dropped

explanation.surface: Someone notes that in hard times the local chippy has cut its prices.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a moment of crisis is read literally: chips (fried potatoes, the 'chips' of British fish and chips) are 'down' in price.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, borrowed from gambling counters on the table, describes a decisive and critical moment.

indicators.note: edited suggests text reworked, so the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A literary note claims T.S. Eliot thought some woman edited a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of ELIOT THOUGHT SHE rearrange into the title of Virginia Woolf's 1927 novel; Eliot as a writer helps the literary misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf's book about the Ramsay family is one of the great modernist novels.

definitions.meaning: earlier or older, as in the earlier-born of two
a church officer, like an ... of a congregation

explanation.surface: Looks like a choice between two church dignitaries, a prior or a prebendary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like a monastic title but works as the adjective meaning earlier or older.
explanation.definitionFit: Older in age is a synonym for prior; a church office-holder is a looser sense matching the prebendary.

definitions.meaning: C is the Roman numeral for a number of tens, ten of them
an old English subdivision of a shire, used for local courts

explanation.surface: Reads like a map key: the letter C stands for a county division.
explanation.walkthrough: The hundred was a historical subdivision of an English county with its own court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman numeral C stands for this number, and medieval England split shires into these administrative units.

parts.note: PREF is a standard abbreviation of preferred, as in preference shares
ABs are able-bodied seamen

explanation.surface: Cheap housing is said to be the choice of seafarers.
explanation.walkthrough: Prefabs were the factory-built bungalows put up across Britain after the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Prefabricated houses were built quickly and cheaply, making them low-cost dwellings.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin, as in £sd
marks and signs are both symbols

explanation.surface: A financial note about moving a shilling into German marks.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin worth a twentieth of a pound; 'Marks' looks like the German currency but means symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign property or rights is to transfer them legally to someone else.

clue.text: Letter from Minneapolis one man left out

indicators.note: left out says the letters for one man are taken from the city's name, and the rest rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A letter posted from Minneapolis, with one man missing from it.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I and MAN out of MINNEAPOLIS and NEPOLIS is left; rearranged, it gives the Greek letter. No separate word signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth character of the Greek alphabet.

definitions.meaning: Father Time is the weathervane above Lord's cricket ground
leaders or rulers with power over others

explanation.surface: A whimsical image of the figure of Time keeping watch over tribal leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Time is the famous weathervane at Lord's, the London cricket ground, so he presides over Lord's.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlords are supreme rulers or lords holding power above lesser chiefs.

clue.text: King of Arms moving Arnold to nursery

indicators.note: moving suggests shifting things around, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arnold, a royal, is being moved into the nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a heraldic title: one of the senior officers of the College of Arms responsible for the north of England and Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Norroy and Ulster is the title of one of the English heralds holding the rank of King of Arms.

parts.note: a set is a television set, and these meals are eaten in front of it

explanation.surface: Looks like a question about fixed-price restaurant menus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' seems to mean fixed, as in a set menu, but refers to the television set.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready meals on a tray are eaten while watching the television, hence meals of the set.

indicators.note: after says the piece for always comes behind the one for street

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A street guide that has always been used.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer something is to direct or guide its course.

clue.text: English county town loses ring — one by a pottery factory

indicators.note: loses says a letter is dropped from the town's name

parts.note: Truro is the county town of Cornwall
a ring is round, like the letter O
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A travel note about an English county town near a pottery works.
explanation.walkthrough: Truro is the county town of Cornwall in south-west England; dropping its last O gives TRUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Etruria was the Staffordshire works and village Josiah Wedgwood built to make his pottery.

clue.text: Astronomer putting sign on old boat, we're told

indicators.note: sign on old boat puts the zodiac sign after the boat, as if added onto it
we're told points to words heard rather than read, so the boat is taken by its sound

parts.note: a galley is an old oared ship
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone attaches a sign to an old ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian scientist who used an early telescope to observe Jupiter's moons was a famed astronomer.

parts.note: a rock cake is a kind of small cake, and a bread roll is another

explanation.surface: Seems to be about a style of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock and roll' suggests the music, but rock cakes and bread rolls are both baked goods of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round baked item can be a rock bun or simply a bread roll.

clue.text: Prevents progress of some slim pedestrians

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Thin walkers somehow hold up the traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: To obstruct or hinder is to stop something moving forward.

clue.text: From whom injured camper gets aid

definitions.text: From whom injured camper gets aid

indicators.note: injured suggests something knocked out of shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Who helps a camper hurt on holiday?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the fodder is CAMPER plus AID, and the clue describes who comes to help.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance medic is the person who gives emergency aid to someone hurt.

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the feet below the earth

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth, as on electrical plugs

explanation.surface: A creature whose feet sit beneath the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, a small amphibian.

parts.note: to squeal is to inform on someone, as is to sing, past tense sang

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for tune runs backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Someone shrieked over a tune and was given a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squealed' looks like a cry but is slang for informed, as 'sang' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine and fruit.

clue.text: Fall ill, having bad weather in the East End

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End drop their H sounds, so the initial letter goes

parts.note: hail is a form of bad weather

explanation.surface: Someone falls ill after enduring bad weather in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End of London is home of the Cockney accent, which drops the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unwell or sickly is the old verb sense of this word.

parts.note: a horn is a feeler or antenna on an insect or snail

indicators.note: askew means crooked, so the three letters following are rearranged

explanation.surface: Insects whose antennae are set at an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Large wasps are stinging insects.

clue.text: In Latin, I stumble over exercise that's self-absorbed

parts.note: ego is the Latin word for I
to trip over something is to stumble on it

explanation.surface: A Latin speaker confesses to tripping over during a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: An activity indulged in to boost one's own vanity is a self-centred outing.

clue.text: Top soldiers joined forces and set out

indicators.note: top in a down clue means the first letter of the word

parts.note: to have allied is to have joined forces

explanation.surface: Elite troops combined armies and marched off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top soldiers' looks like a phrase for an elite unit but just gives the first letter of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To sally is to rush out or set forth, as on a sortie.

indicators.note: otherwise expressed says the letters of the last word are put a different way

explanation.surface: A synonym given another way for spoiled or soiled.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: rearranging SULLIED gives the answer, and sullied is itself close in meaning to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treated badly or abused has been spoiled, much as sullied things have.

clue.text: Almost 2.54cm, bit of iron's on gold tooth

indicators.note: almost says the measurement's word loses its last letter

parts.note: an inch is 2.54 centimetres
a bit of iron is its first letter, with the 's added
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A dental note about a tiny piece of iron on a gold tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: The cutting front teeth of the mouth are these.

clue.text: Types of window allowing smoke to escape

definitions.text: Types of window allowing smoke to escape

parts.words: Types of window allowing smoke to escape
parts.note: slatted openings first made in medieval roofs to let hearth smoke out

explanation.surface: A description of windows that let smoke out.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for slatted vents first named the roof turret over a medieval hall hearth that let smoke out.
explanation.definitionFit: Windows or vents with angled slats let air and smoke pass while keeping rain out.

clue.text: Beard having a couple of points

parts.note: west, one compass point, abbreviated W
north, another compass point, abbreviated N

explanation.surface: A beard with two sharp tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beard' here is the bristly growth on an ear of barley or other grass, not facial hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The bristle on a grain head such as barley is called its beard.

clue.text: Poor actor's part as expressed on picnic menu

parts.note: a ham is an overacting, poor actor

indicators.note: as expressed signals the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: An actor's part is written up on a picnic menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A bread bun filled with sliced pork is a sandwich typical of picnics.

indicators.note: overheard means heard, pointing to a word with the same sound

parts.note: counsel means advice

explanation.surface: The advice an assembly gave was overheard.
explanation.definitionFit: A local authority's governing body is an elected gathering of members.

clue.text: The Macnabs, say, taking ecstasy. No!

definitions.text: The Macnabs, say, taking ecstasy. No!

indicators.note: taking means the family group takes in the drug's letter

parts.note: the Macnabs are a Scottish clan, an example of one
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Outrage at a Highland family taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay puts E inside CLAN; the 'No!' then turns the whole into a refusal of drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off drugs is called being clean, the opposite of taking ecstasy.

parts.note: UN is the French indefinite article
DER is a German definite article

explanation.surface: Fewer than two items while travelling overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Below a figure is a synonym for fewer than it.

indicators.note: revolutionary hints at turning things over, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tireless rebel, beyond doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of UNRESTING is itself described by the clue: a rebel who never rests.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel in arms against authority is a restless revolutionary figure.

parts.note: a lag is a convict, and to lag also means to stay behind; this convict would not stay

explanation.surface: Someone who refuses to fall behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Lag means a convict, and also to hang back; this convict did not wait around inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict who has broken out of jail is one who refused to stay put.
